SAR and PolSAR images (R6)

Source: R/image.R
SARImage.Rd

SARImage stores a SAR image as an array of dimension nrow x ncol x layers. Two types are supported:

"polsar"

a complex array whose p = m(m+1)/2 layers are the distinct entries of the \(m \times m\) covariance matrix of each pixel, in the order \(C_{11}, \ldots, C_{mm}, C_{12}, C_{13}, \ldots\) (for \(m = 3\): HH, HV, VV, HH.HV*, HH.VV*, HV.VV*), as in SanFrancisco150;

"intensity"

a real (or real-valued complex) array whose layers are intensity channels.

The class offers cropping, Pauli colour composition, plotting, local (moving-window) features for classification, entropy maps and conversion to tibbles.

Public fields

data

The image array.

type

"polsar" or "intensity".

channels

Names of the intensity channels.

looks

Nominal number of looks (optional, NULL if unknown).

Active bindings

nrow

Number of rows (read-only).

ncol

Number of columns (read-only).

m

Number of channels; matrix order for PolSAR images (read-only).

SARImage$new()

Create a SAR image.

Usage

SARImage$new(data, type = NULL, looks = NULL, channels = NULL)

Arguments

data

Array nrow x ncol x layers (a matrix is treated as a single intensity channel).

type

"polsar" or "intensity". Guessed when NULL: complex arrays with m(m+1)/2 layers (m >= 2) and non-zero imaginary parts are PolSAR images.

looks

Nominal number of looks.

channels

Names of the intensity channels.

SARImage$intensity()

Intensity of one channel.

Usage

SARImage$intensity(channel = 1)

Arguments

channel

Channel index or name.

SARImage$intensities()

All intensity channels as a real array.

Usage

SARImage$intensities()

SARImage$crop()

Crop the image.

Usage

SARImage$crop(rows, cols)

Arguments

rows, cols

Row and column indices to keep.

SARImage$pixel()

Observation at a pixel: the Hermitian covariance matrix (PolSAR) or the vector of intensities.

Usage

SARImage$pixel(row, col)

Arguments

row, col

Pixel position.

SARImage$window()

Observations inside a square window centred at a pixel (truncated at the borders). Returns an n x layers matrix.

Usage

SARImage$window(row, col, window = 3)

Arguments

row, col

Pixel position.

window

Odd window side.

SARImage$pauli()

Pauli RGB composition scaled to [0, 1] (PolSAR images with three channels); for other images the first three intensities are used.

Usage

SARImage$pauli(stretch = 0.98, gamma = 0.5)

Arguments

stretch

Upper quantile used for linear stretching.

gamma

Gamma correction exponent.

Examples

img <- SARImage$new(SanFrancisco150, looks = 4)
img
#> <SARImage> 150 x 150 PolSAR (3 x 3 covariance)
#>   channels: HH, HV, VV
#>   looks: 4
#>   mean HH  = 0.1735
#>   mean HV  = 0.04224
#>   mean VV  = 0.147
small <- img$crop(1:40, 1:40)
dim(small$intensities())
#> [1] 40 40  3
small$pixel(1, 1)
#>                            [,1]                       [,2]
#> [1,] 0.0049587982+0.0000000000i 0.0006074079-0.0001119103i
#> [2,] 0.0006074079+0.0001119103i 0.0003967038+0.0000000000i
#> [3,] 0.0113060614-0.0013223464i 0.0011964096-0.0005374640i
#>                         [,3]
#> [1,] 0.01130606+0.001322346i
#> [2,] 0.00119641+0.000537464i
#> [3,] 0.02823210+0.000000000i
head(small$features(window = 3))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 20
#>     row   col mean_HH  mean_HV mean_VV   cov_HH_HH cov_HH_HV cov_HH_VV cov_HV_HV
#>   <int> <int>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1     1     1 0.00596 0.000472  0.0233 0.00000666    8.51e-8   2.08e-5   9.50e-9
#> 2     2     1 0.00588 0.000528  0.0224 0.00000536   -2.69e-8   1.74e-5   1.68e-8
#> 3     3     1 0.00526 0.000556  0.0206 0.00000457    6.27e-8   1.60e-5   1.43e-8
#> 4     4     1 0.00485 0.000490  0.0190 0.00000213    1.74e-8   6.28e-6   3.16e-8
#> 5     5     1 0.00427 0.000413  0.0177 0.000000935   3.21e-8   1.79e-6   1.56e-8
#> 6     6     1 0.00400 0.000462  0.0159 0.000000755  -1.35e-8   4.27e-7   4.03e-8
#> # ℹ 11 more variables: cov_HV_VV <dbl>, cov_VV_VV <dbl>, c11 <dbl>, c22 <dbl>,
#> #   c33 <dbl>, c12_re <dbl>, c12_im <dbl>, c13_re <dbl>, c13_im <dbl>,
#> #   c23_re <dbl>, c23_im <dbl>
